disease_label: заболевание спектра синдрома Ретта (Rett syndrome spectrum disorder / Rett-like syndrome)
source_title: Клинический случай пациента школьного возраста с заболеванием спектра синдрома Ретта и делецией в гене MECP2

variants.variant_type: frameshift deletion (deletion of 228 nucleotides, NM_004992.4; heterozygous deletion of chromosome X segment 154030384–154030612)
variants.clinical_significance: pathogenic (described in female patients with variable Rett syndrome course, OMIM 312750, in some cases associated with pharmacoresistant epilepsy)
variants.domain: C-terminal domain (codon 406, downstream of TRD aa 201-310)

expected_evidence.value: заболевание спектра синдрома Ретта (Rett syndrome spectrum disorder / Rett-like syndrome)
frameshift deletion (deletion of 228 nucleotides, NM_004992.4; heterozygous deletion of chromosome X segment 154030384–154030612)
C-terminal domain (codon 406, downstream of TRD aa 201-310)

developmental regression after period of normal/delayed early development; delayed motor development (head control 3.5 mo, sitting 8 mo, walking 1 year 7 months); ataxia / cerebellar gait disturbance; delayed speech development (first words at 2.5 years), loss of speech; moderate intellectual disability (Wechsler IQ 44); pharmacoresistant epilepsy (atonic, myoclonic, tonic, bilateral tonic-clonic seizures; reflex seizures provoked by sound/touch); diffuse muscular hypotonia; brisk lower-limb tendon reflexes, bilateral Babinski sign; hand stereotypies (waving, hand shaking, finger fumbling); loss of acquired purposeful hand and motor skills; truncal ataxia, dysmetria, intention tremor; loss of ability to walk and stand independently; cerebellar volume reduction / hypoplasia of vermis and cerebellar hemispheres on MRI; lethargy and reduced activity / drowsiness; loss of toileting skills and feeding ability (required nasogastric/gastrostomy feeding); transient elevation of blood ammonia (152.6 µmol/L) and lactate (4.8 mmol/L)
early childhood with developmental delay; seizure onset at 7 years; severe regression at 9-10 years
unknown (born to healthy non-consanguineous parents, healthy sibling; de novo status not explicitly confirmed for the MECP2 deletion)
